title: Two-act live spark: underspecified escalation tiers
description: Act 1: a headless Claude Code agent authors tasks/escalation.py from the task_spec below, which is plausible but incomplete — it documents only the 14-day staleness window. A hidden Bazel test (hidden_validation) encodes the full requirement, including a second 60-day escalation window the spec never mentions; the agent cannot see it (the CLI runs in an empty scratch directory and the test is written only into the temporary validation workspace). Real `bazel test` through the NativeLink cache catches the gap: the red leg is the agent's honest best effort failing a requirement it was never told, not scripted corruption. Act 2: the agent receives the recorded bazel failure excerpt from Act 1's flight-recorder artifacts and produces the fix.

design_honesty.what_the_agent_saw: Exactly task_spec plus the read-only context_files contents plus output_contract, assembled deterministically by nlfr.spark.build_act1_prompt; verify any receipt's prompt_sha256 by rebuilding that prompt from this file and a pristine demo workspace.
design_honesty.what_the_agent_could_not_see: hidden_validation (the second 60-day window test) — written only into the temp validation workspace; the agent CLI cwd is an empty scratch directory.
design_honesty.why_the_failure_is_honest: The hidden requirement extends the spec where it is silent (behavior past 60 days); it never contradicts the visible spec. The failure comes from executing the agent's real output under real bazel test.
design_honesty.first_pass_success_policy: If the agent passes on the first try, the run is recorded and kept honestly; rerun under a new run group. All runs are kept.
design_honesty.retry_policy: rerun = new run group; no recorded run is discarded or overwritten

workspace_overrides.reason: The demo template's MODULE.bazel carries a git_override on nativelink's local-remote-execution module (added for the Linux LRE track). Cache-only validation never uses LRE, and on this host that module cannot analyze under any available bazel: the template's pinned bazel 7.4.1 fails its rules_rs >=7.7.0 compatibility floor, while bazel >=7.7.0 rejects the module's rust_toolchain attributes. The temp validation workspace pins the module-free configuration that was proven green for cache-only runs; this override is recorded with its SHA-256 in the workspace setup hashes.
content_lines: # Two-act spark validation workspace: module-free cache-only configuration.
# The demo template's local-remote-execution git_override is stripped here;

task_spec: Create the module tasks/escalation.py for the tasks triage library. Implement escalation_tier(score, age_days) -> str returning one of 'p0', 'p1', or 'p2'. The base tier comes from the numeric score using the thresholds in tasks.policy: scores at or above URGENT_THRESHOLD are 'p0', scores at or above NORMAL_THRESHOLD are 'p1', anything lower is 'p2'. Stale tasks escalate: once a task's age_days reaches the 14-day staleness window it moves up one tier. Escalation saturates at 'p0'. Import the thresholds from tasks.policy; use only the Python standard library.
output_contract: Respond with exactly one fenced Python code block containing the complete content of tasks/escalation.py, and no other code blocks. Do not use any tools. Do not include explanations before or after beyond a single short sentence.

hidden_validation.note: Full requirement: a second escalation window at 60 days, omitted from task_spec on purpose. Consistent with the spec (which is silent past the first window), so a faithful best-effort implementation of the spec fails here honestly.
content_lines: """Full escalation requirement; the underspecified brief omits the second window.
Bazel py_test executes this file as a plain script, so the checks run under
unittest.main() — bare test functions would silently pass without executing.
# Operational convention the 14-day brief never mentions: tasks aging
# past the 60-day window escalate one further tier.

act1.expected: red validation leg: hidden escalation_policy_test fails against the agent's honest best-effort implementation; priority_test passes and populates the NativeLink cache

act2.evidence_source: Act 1 recorded artifacts (bazel stderr/stdout excerpt via nlfr.spark.failure_excerpt) — the recorder's own evidence is the agent's debugging context
act2.expected: green validation leg: corrected module passes; unchanged targets see warm NativeLink cache hits

proof_claims.statement: Act 1 failure comes from real bazel test execution of the agent's real output against a hidden requirement the visible spec omits.
Agent provenance carries a CLI receipt: server-resolved model id, session id, token usage, response SHA-256, prompt SHA-256; the raw prompt is never stored.
Act 2 debugging context is an excerpt of Act 1's recorded artifacts, not a re-run; the fix validates green with warm cache hits on unchanged targets.
